verdict: Fly.io: Choose Fly.io when PAYG microVM/app hosting is the job — not Render by default, and not Cloudways managed VMs. Scores use the IT & Development editorial methodology from first-party research as of 2026-08-18 — not hands-on product testing.
strengths: Clear PaaS identity vs managed WP
Support SKU documented separately from hosting
weaknesses: No free plan for new accounts
Easy to confuse $29 Support with hosting
bestFor: Teams that want PAYG microVM/app hosting close to users
Buyers comparing Fly.io $1.94 shared-cpu-1x to Render Pro $25 + compute
Orgs that will not treat $29 Support as the hosting SKU
notIdealFor: Teams that want Render’s simpler git-push dashboard as the default award path
Managed WordPress or Cloudways VM buyers (landscape)
tradeoffs: Per-agent vs per-host vs per-seat vs per-GB pricing models
Module stacking and consumption overages vs single-SKU floors
Free tiers vs enterprise SSO/audit gates
Landscape-adjacent tools vs primary job-cluster peers on best pages
recommendation: Choose Fly.io when PAYG microVM/app hosting is the job — not Render by default, and not Cloudways managed VMs. Compare Render for the cloud-paas award path; Cloudways only on landscape pages for managed VMs; WP Engine for managed WordPress.
editorialNotes: IT optional-next batch. Approved on it-development-editorial v1.0.0. membershipRole=primary. jobCluster=cloud-paas. handsOnTesting=false. Affiliate economics excluded.

overallScoreRationale: Weighted average of the eight IT editorial criteria using category weights (IT job fit 16, workflow depth 14, ease of use 12, integrations 12, admin/security 12, value 12, AI 12, scalability 10), rounded to 1 decimal. Products are scored inside their job cluster — ITSM, observability, source control, hosting panels, and web-data platforms are not forced into one undifferentiated ranking. Not a hands-on lab score, and affiliate economics are excluded.
